evals.prompt: We have an incident. Since about 14:05 Lisbon time the checkout API is returning 5xx: Grafana shows ~12% of POST /api/checkout failing on edge-01 and edge-02 (window 14:05-14:20, still ongoing). checkout-svc v2.31 was deployed at 13:58. The payments provider status page is green. Rui is on call and is checking the DB pool graphs; Marta (DBA) says DB CPU is at 30%. No customer comms have gone out yet. Write the live incident report and a short email to the leadership team in Portuguese (they're in Lisbon). I'm Gabriel, the incident lead.
evals.expected_output: A live incident report (not a postmortem) plus a ready-to-send PT-PT email draft. Nothing sent.
assertions: [Substance] The v2.31 deploy is presented as a hypothesis/candidate, not as the root cause
[Substance] No invented facts: no version numbers, times, owners, commitments, impact or customer figures that are not in the prompt (placeholders and 'unknown' are fine)
[Substance] Figures are consistent between the live report and the email (≈12%, 14:05, 13:58, 14:05-14:20 window)
[Substance] Output does not claim that the email or any update was sent
[House] Live report separates known, suspected, ruled out and unknown (or equivalent labels)
[House] The report states one timezone for its timestamps
[House] No 'MTTR' (or 'mean time to ...') label is used for this single incident
[House] No severity level is assigned or proposed (severity is out of scope)
[House] Live report is in English (the user's language); only the email is in Portuguese
[House] Email body is Portuguese from Portugal (no Brazilian forms such as 'equipe', 'time' meaning team, 'usuário', 'você', gerund progressive)
[House] Email uses 'Resumo:' (or equivalent summary heading) rather than 'Causa Raiz:' since the cause is unconfirmed
[House] Email contains a DETAILS section after the closing
[House] Every next-step action in the email has a bracketed owner or an explicit to-be-assigned placeholder

evals.prompt: Checkout was failing on 30 Sep for ~40 minutes around lunchtime. The evidence is in the inputs folder: HAProxy log from edge-01, a Grafana metrics export, the change log and the on-call notes. Find the root cause and tell me how confident we can be. Ana thinks it was the CDN cert rotation.
evals.expected_output: An RCA identifying the DB pool reduction (config v14, 50->10) as the mechanism, dismissing the CDN hypothesis with evidence, with an explicit confidence level.
assertions: [Substance] Identifies the checkout-svc config v14 DB pool reduction (50 -> 10) as the trigger/cause
[Substance] Rejects or demotes the CDN certificate rotation hypothesis citing evidence (e.g. only be_checkout affected, sQ queue timeouts, cart unaffected, timing)
[Substance] Explicitly reconciles the UTC HAProxy timestamps with the Lisbon (UTC+1) change log/metrics
[Substance] Notes that recovery after rollback supports but does not by itself prove the cause, or proposes a discriminating test
[Substance] Mentions the evidence gap that the edge-02 log is missing
[Substance] Treats the DBA 'DB is fine' statement as reported/unverified, or checks it against the CPU metric
[Substance] No invented facts (no metrics, owners, times or changes absent from the inputs)
[Substance] Every figure that appears more than once matches, and each stated percentage equals its stated count/total
[House] States confidence using one of: confirmed, strongly supported, unconfirmed, unknown
[House] Separates trigger, root cause/mechanism and contributing conditions

evals.prompt: Review my branch feature/pricing-refactor against main before I merge. The repo is inputs/billing-svc.
evals.expected_output: A findings-first review flagging the cross-tenant read, SQL injection, N+1 and rounding change, without modifying the repo.
assertions: [Substance] Flags removal of tenant scoping in get_invoice as a blocking/high-priority defect (any scale)
[Substance] Flags the f-string status filter in search_invoices as SQL injection, blocking/high-priority (any scale)
[Substance] Flags the per-line product price lookup as an N+1 query
[Substance] Flags the rounding change (int(total) truncation vs per-line round) as a money/correctness defect
[Substance] No false-positive findings: every reported defect is real in the changed code
[Substance] Repository left unchanged: same HEAD, branch and clean working tree
[House] Findings use P0-P3 priority labels
[House] Each finding cites a file:line location
[House] Contains no style-only findings (naming, formatting, docstrings, commit messages)
[House] States the comparison/merge base or the reviewed range

evals.prompt: INC-2219 from Monday 28 Sep: checkout payment confirmations were failing for roughly an hour mid-morning. Everything we exported is in the inputs folder: both HAProxy edge logs, the payments-gw IIS log, Grafana exports for fraud-svc, checkout-svc and the orders DB, the change log and our Slack notes. People are blaming the DB failover and the CDN change. I need the root cause, how sure we are, the impact in numbers, and what actually fixed it.
evals.expected_output: RCA attributing failures to payments-gw v5.2 synchronous fraud check (3 s timeout) combined with fraud-svc minReplicas cut and campaign load; DB failover and CDN ruled out; edge-02 clock offset detected; impact quantified; flag-off identified as the fix.
assertions: [Substance] Identifies payments-gw v5.2 synchronous fraud check (flag fraud_check_sync, 3 s timeout) as the enabling change / trigger
[Substance] Identifies the fraud-svc minReplicas cut (6 -> 2) as a contributing condition or co-cause
[Substance] Identifies the campaign traffic increase as a contributing condition
[Substance] Rules out the DB failover with evidence (≈20 s blip at 10:05 Lisbon, after onset, different failure signature)
[Substance] Rules out the CDN Brotli change with evidence (static assets only / only the confirm path affected)
[Substance] Detects the edge-02 clock offset (about +95 s) and corrects or excludes it
[Substance] Notes that only /api/checkout/confirm (payment path) was materially affected
[Substance] Quantifies impact with a denominator (failed vs total confirm requests, or a failure rate over the window)
[Substance] Identifies flag fraud_check_sync OFF as what ended the impact, with scaling fraud-svc as a partial mitigation
[Substance] Reconciles UTC logs with Lisbon (UTC+1) change log, notes and metrics
[Substance] Does not add edge 503s and gateway 504s into one failure total unless it shows they are distinct events (or labels the sum as an upper bound)
[Substance] Every figure that appears more than once matches, and each stated percentage equals its stated count/total
[Substance] No invented facts (no metrics, owners, times or changes absent from the inputs)
[House] States confidence using one of: confirmed, strongly supported, unconfirmed, unknown
